name: Nakti Wak (Pork with Dry Fish)
ingredients: 500g pork belly, cut into medium cubes
50g dried fish (usually fermented or salted fish like Ngari)
instructions: 1. Clean the dry fish thoroughly and soak in warm water for 10 minutes to remove excess salt.
2. Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or wok until smoking point, then lower the heat.
3. Add onions and sauté until translucent, then stir in ginger-garlic paste and green chilies.
4. Add the pork cubes and sear until lightly browned, stirring in the turmeric and salt.
5. Add the prepared dry fish to the pot and stir well to incorporate the flavors.
6. Pour in the water, cover the pot, and simmer on low heat for 30-40 minutes until the pork is tender and the liquid has reduced to a thick gravy.
7. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot with steamed red rice.
description: Nakti Wak is a quintessential dish from the Garo community of Meghalaya. It highlights the regional preference for fermented and dried ingredients, which provide a distinct, umami-rich depth to pork dishes. It represents the indigenous culinary heritage of the hills, where preservation techniques like drying fish are essential to the traditional diet.
